The 2024 Arizona Cardinals finished 8-9 over 17 games, scoring 400 points and allowing 379 for a point differential of +21. The offense ranked 11th in EPA per play at +0.07, while the defense ranked 26th at +0.05. The team averaged 23.5 points per game (12th of 32) and allowed 22.3 (15th of 32). Final full-season DVOA was +8.8% overall (12th of 32), +8.4% on offense (11th), −0.6% on defense (14th, where lower is better) and −0.2% on special teams (18th).

Kyler Murray threw for 3851 yards with 21 TD and 11 INT over 541 attempts, posting an NGS CPOE of +2.2 (12th of 43) and an EPA per dropback of +0.11 (18th of 52). James Conner carried 236 times for 1094 yards. Trey McBride led the receivers with 147 targets and 1146 yards, and Marvin Harrison Jr. had 116 targets, 885 yards and 8 TD. Elijah Higgins was the most efficient target at +0.40 EPA per target on 24 targets. The offensive line allowed a 15% pressure rate (2nd of 32) and a 5% sack rate (5th).

Zaven Collins led the defense with 5 sacks and 12 pressures, and Dante Stills had 4.5 sacks. The Cardinals produced 7.1 pressures per game (26th of 32). The safety group allowed a 124.7 rating (32nd of 32), Starling Thomas allowed 101.2 on 55 targets, and the team passer rating allowed was 100.8 (23rd). Chad Ryland made 28 of 32 field goals, and Matt Prater made 6 of 6.

The 2024 Falcons went 8-9 with a point differential of −34 (389 points scored, 423 allowed). The offense ranked 13th in EPA per play, but the defense ranked 27th in EPA per play allowed. Final full-season DVOA (the sheet's latest FTN table) put Atlanta 20th overall (−7.3%), 14th on offense (+4.4%), 29th on defense (+7.5%, where lower is better) and 29th on special teams (−4.1%).

Kirk Cousins was accurate (NGS CPOE +3.4, 5th of 43) but only average in production (EPA per dropback +0.04, 24th of 52), with 16 interceptions. The scheme stood out: the Falcons used motion on 63% of plays (5th), and shotgun play action produced +0.57 EPA (1st) and 11.7 yards per play (1st), while under-center play action fell to −0.18 (30th). Bijan Robinson (1456 yards, 4.8 per carry, +0.68 RYOE) was the engine, Darnell Mooney was the most efficient target (+0.41 EPA per target), and Drake London (1271 yards, 9 touchdowns) led the receivers. The line allowed a 20% pressure rate (9th) and a 5% sack rate (8th).

The defense was the problem: 31 sacks, a 5% sack rate (31st of 32, where 1 = highest) and 7.8 pressures per game. Arnold Ebiketie led with 6 sacks and 24 pressures, Matt Judon had 5.5 sacks, and Kaden Elliss added 5 sacks with 16 QB hits. The cornerbacks were the worst group in the league, ranked 32nd in rating allowed at 107.3, and the team passer rating allowed was 102.3 (26th). Special teams lagged at −4.1% DVOA (29th).

The 2024 Ravens went 12-5 with a +157 point differential (518 scored, 361 allowed), averaging 30.5 points per game (3rd) and allowing 21.2 (9th). The offense ranked first in EPA per play (+0.22), and the defense eighth (−0.05, 1 = lowest allowed). The final full-season DVOA was +41.4%, the league's best, with the offense at +35.1% (1st), the defense at −8.1% (6th) and special teams at −1.9% (23rd).

Lamar Jackson threw for 4172 yards, 41 TD and 4 INT (119.6 rating) with +0.36 EPA per dropback (2nd of 52), though his NGS CPOE was −0.2 (26th of 43) and his time to throw of 3.14 s ranked 43rd of 43. Derrick Henry was the engine: 1921 yards at 5.9 per carry with a +1.77 RYOE (1st). Mark Andrews was the most efficient target (+0.73 EPA per target, 11 TD on 69 targets). Play action from under center produced +0.56 EPA (1st), and heavy sets led the league at +0.24 EPA.

Kyle Van Noy (12.5 sacks, 21 QB hits) and Odafe Oweh (10 sacks, 28 pressures) led a front that produced 54 sacks (8%, 5th), with Nnamdi Madubuike adding 6.5. The cornerback group allowed a 69.1 rating (1st), with Marlon Humphrey at 60.9 and Nate Wiggins at 66.7. Deep passes (+0.39 EPA, 20th) and linebacker coverage (111.0, 31st) were the soft spots. Special teams were below average, though Justin Tucker went only 22 of 30 on field goals.

Buffalo finished 13-4 with a +157 point differential (525 points for, 368 against). The offense ranked 2nd in EPA per play (+0.19) and 2nd in points per game (30.9), while the defense ranked 12th in EPA per play allowed (−0.01) and tied for 11th in points allowed per game (21.6). Final DVOA placed the Bills 4th overall (+22.7%), 2nd on offense (+20.7%), 11th on defense (−4.7%, lower is better) and 28th on special teams (−2.7%).

Josh Allen posted 3731 yards, 28 TD and 6 INT, with +0.30 EPA per dropback (4th of 52) and +0.47 EPA per carry on 51 runs. His 2.89 s time to throw ranked 31st of 43, but his pressure-to-sack rate was just 16% (league 31%), and the line allowed pressure on 16% of dropbacks (3rd of 32) with a 2% sack rate (1st). James Cook carried 207 times for 1009 yards (4.9 YPC, +0.82 RYOE). Khalil Shakir (100 targets, 821 yards, +0.44 EPA per target) and Keon Coleman (57 targets, 556 yards, +0.44) led the receivers. Presnap motion on 51% of plays produced +0.29 EPA (1st), and heavy sets produced +0.65 pass EPA (1st).

Gregory Rousseau led the defense with 8 sacks, 24 QB hits and 36 pressures, and A.J. Epenesa added 6 sacks. The team totaled only 39 sacks at a 6% rate (20th). The secondary was the soft spot: Rasul Douglas allowed a 122.0 rating with 4 TD, and the cornerbacks ranked 24th (99.1) and safeties 20th (102.9). Special teams ranked 28th in DVOA.

The 2024 Panthers went 5-12 with a point differential of −193 (341 points scored, 534 allowed). The offense ranked 22nd in EPA per play, but the defense ranked 32nd, last in the league, in EPA per play allowed. Final full-season DVOA (the sheet's latest FTN table) put Carolina 30th overall (−32.9%), 24th on offense (−11.6%), 32nd and last on defense (+19.2%, where lower is better) and 25th on special teams (−2.1%).

Bryce Young posted NGS CPOE +2.1 (13th of 43) and was aggressive (19.8%, 4th), but his EPA per dropback was −0.03 (34th of 52) over 450 dropbacks, and the line allowed a 24% pressure rate (26th). Andy Dalton's 173 dropbacks produced −0.14 (45th of 52). Chuba Hubbard was the bright spot, with 1195 yards, 4.8 per carry and +1.11 RYOE (4th of 47). Adam Thielen was the most efficient target (+0.65 EPA per target on 62 targets), while Diontae Johnson (−0.22 EPA per target, YAC+ 128th of 129) struggled.

The defense was the worst in the league by EPA, with 32 sacks, a 5% sack rate (29th of 32, where 1 = highest) and 5.9 pressures per game (31st of 32, where 1 = most). Jadeveon Clowney and A'Shawn Robinson each had 5.5 sacks, and D.J. Wonnum added 4. The pass defense allowed a 108.1 team passer rating (32nd), with cornerbacks (106.1, 30th) and safeties (111.7, 27th) both poor. Special teams were 25th in DVOA (−2.1%), and the unit committed 25 penalties for 190 yards, the most in the league.

The 2024 Chicago Bears went 5-12 with a point differential of −60, scoring 310 points (18.2 per game, 28th of 32) and allowing 370. The offense ranked 26th of 32 in EPA per play (−0.08), while the defense ranked 14th of 32 in EPA per play allowed (+0.01, where lower is better). Final FTN DVOA was 25th of 32 overall at −12.7%: offense −13.1% (27th of 32), defense +3.7% (22nd of 32, where lower is better), special teams +4.1% (5th of 32).

Caleb Williams threw 20 touchdowns and 6 interceptions, but his NGS CPOE was −1.1 (28th of 43) and his EPA per dropback was −0.04 (35th of 52). The line was the root cause: 68 sacks allowed, a 10% sack rate (32nd of 32) and a 23% pressure rate (22nd of 32). D'Andre Swift ran 253 times for 959 yards at −0.15 EPA per carry. DJ Moore led the receivers with 140 targets. Play action from under center was the one productive look, at +0.10 EPA per dropback versus −0.09 without it.

Montez Sweat led the front with 5.5 sacks and 21 pressures, and Gervon Dexter had 5 sacks and a team-high 19 QB hits. The team recorded 40 sacks (7% sack rate, 10th of 32). The linebackers were the best coverage unit (80.0 rating allowed, 2nd of 32), while the safeties ranked 31st of 32 (123.0 rating). The defense allowed 8.5 yards per target, the most in the league. Special teams were a bright spot, ranking 5th of 32 in DVOA.

The 2024 Bengals went 9-8 with a +38 point differential (472 points scored, 434 allowed), averaging 27.8 points per game (6th) and allowing 25.5 (25th, tied). The offense ranked seventh in EPA per play (+0.09) and the defense 22nd (+0.04, 1 = lowest allowed). The final full-season DVOA was +7.0% (13th), with the offense at +14.0% (5th), the defense at +6.4% (27th) and special teams at −0.5% (20th). The team was built on a pass-first offense (PROE +11.1, 1st).

Joe Burrow was excellent: 4918 yards, 43 TD, 9 INT and a 108.5 rating, with a +4.5 NGS CPOE (3rd of 43) and +0.17 EPA per dropback (11th of 52). Ja'Marr Chase (1708 yards, 17 TD) and Tee Higgins (+0.52 EPA per target on 109) led the receivers, and Mike Gesicki caught 65 passes for 665 yards. Chase Brown ran 229 times for 990 yards at 4.3 per carry. Play action from under center was used on only 4% of dropbacks (31st). The line allowed pressure on 21% of dropbacks (17th).

Trey Hendrickson was the pass rush (17.5 sacks, 36 QB hits, 54 pressures), with Joseph Ossai adding 5 sacks, but the team's 36 sacks came at a 6% rate (27th). Passer rating allowed was 95.5 (17th), with the cornerbacks at 93.0 (17th). Cam Taylor-Britt (98.0 rating, 3 INT) was the most-targeted corner with 91 targets. The run defense (+0.00 EPA per rush, 28th) and the red zone (72% of trips ended in touchdowns, 31st) were the weakest areas.

The 2024 Browns went 3-14 with a −177 point differential (258 points scored, 435 allowed). They averaged 15.2 points per game, the fewest in the league (32nd), and their offense ranked last in EPA per play (−0.19) and in offense DVOA (−31.7%). The final full-season DVOA was −39.9% (32nd) overall, with the defense at +4.0% (25th) and special teams at −4.2% (30th). The offense gave the ball away 34 times against 12 takeaways and allowed 66 sacks (9%, 31st).

Jameis Winston threw for 2121 yards, 13 TD and 12 INT (80.6 rating) with a −2.3 NGS CPOE (35th of 43). Deshaun Watson managed 1148 yards, 5 TD, 3 INT and a 79.0 rating, but his EPA per dropback was −0.21 (49th of 52). Dorian Thompson-Robinson was last at −0.52 (52nd of 52). Jerome Ford was the best back (5.4 yards per carry, +1.10 RYOE, 5th) and Jerry Jeudy the most efficient target (+0.27 EPA per target on 145). The line allowed pressure on 25% of dropbacks (31st).

Myles Garrett led the front with 14 sacks, 28 QB hits and 44 pressures, with Za'Darius Smith (5 sacks) the other main rusher, and the team totaled 41 sacks (7%, 8th). The linebackers were the strength, with a 77.1 coverage rating (1st). The secondary was the clear problem: the cornerback group allowed a 104.1 rating (28th), the safeties 122.1 (30th). Martin Emerson (100.1 rating, 5 TD) was the most-targeted corner. Special teams were weak too, at −4.2% DVOA (30th), with Dustin Hopkins going 18 of 27 on field goals.

Dallas went 7-10 and scored 350 while allowing 468, a differential of −118. The offense ranked 29th in EPA per play at −0.11, and the defense ranked 30th at +0.08. In the final full-season FTN DVOA table, the Cowboys ranked 24th overall at −11.6%, 25th on offense at −12.3%, 24th on defense at +3.9%, and 3rd on special teams at +4.6%.

Cooper Rush threw for 1844 yards with 12 touchdowns, 5 interceptions and an 83.8 rating in 308 attempts, with an NGS CPOE of −5.6 (41st of 43). Dak Prescott threw for 1978 yards with 11 touchdowns, 8 interceptions and an 86.0 rating, with a CPOE of +1.9 (14th of 43). Rico Dowdle gained 1079 yards on 235 carries, averaging 4.6 per carry. CeeDee Lamb led the receivers with 1194 yards and 6 touchdowns, and Jalen Tolbert caught 49 passes for 610 yards and 7 touchdowns. Offense EPA per dropback was −0.04 with play action and −0.12 without. The offensive line allowed a 22% pressure rate, ranked 19th of 32, and a 6% sack rate, ranked 10th.

The defense recorded 52 sacks, a 9% sack rate ranked 2nd. Micah Parsons led with 12 sacks, 23 QB hits and 45 pressures, followed by Chauncey Golston with 5.5 sacks and Carl Lawson with 5. Pressures per game were 10.8, ranked 3rd. Coverage allowed a 104.9 team rating (30th), with cornerbacks at 106.8 (31st). Brandon Aubrey made 40 of 47 field goals with a long of 65, and KaVontae Turpin returned 27 kickoffs for 904 yards.

Denver went 10-7, scoring 425 points and allowing 311 for a differential of +114. The offense ranked 14th of 32 at an EPA per play of +0.02, while the defense led the league at −0.12, ranked 1st where 1 means the lowest allowed. Final DVOA was +16.3%, 6th of 32: offense −0.4% (16th), defense −12.4% (4th) and special teams +4.4% (4th).

Bo Nix threw 29 touchdowns against 12 interceptions, with an EPA per dropback of +0.06, 22nd of 52, though his CPOE of −2.6 ranked 36th of 43. Courtland Sutton drew 135 targets for 1081 yards, and Devaughn Vele was the most efficient target at +0.64 on 55. Javonte Williams ran 139 times for 513 yards, but his RYOE of −0.60 ranked 45th of 47. The line was strong in protection, with a 4% sack rate, 2nd of 32, and a 16% pressure rate, 4th. Play action from shotgun was a strength: 13% of dropbacks, 5th of 32, for an EPA of +0.35, 6th.

Nik Bonitto led the pass rush with 13.5 sacks and 24 quarterback hits, Jonathon Cooper added 10.5 sacks, and Zach Allen posted 8.5 sacks and the team-high 47 pressures. Denver totaled 63 sacks at a 9% rate, 1st of 32, and 12.0 pressures per game, also 1st. Patrick Surtain II allowed a rating of 57.6 on 62 targets with 4 interceptions. Penalties hurt: defensive back penalties totaled 29 for 364 yards, 30th of 32. Special teams were strong at +4.4%, 4th, and Wil Lutz made 31 of 34 field goals.

The 2024 Detroit Lions went 15-2 with a point differential of +222, scoring 564 points (33.2 per game, 1st of 32) and allowing 342 (20.1 per game, 7th of 32). The offense ranked 3rd of 32 in EPA per play (+0.17), and the defense ranked 6th of 32 in EPA per play allowed (−0.06, where lower is better). Final FTN DVOA was 2nd of 32 overall at +34.8%: offense +19.9% (3rd of 32), defense −9.5% (5th of 32, where lower is better), special teams +5.4% (1st of 32).

Jared Goff threw 37 touchdowns and 12 interceptions with a 111.8 rating, a +5.1 NGS CPOE (2nd of 43) and +0.28 EPA per dropback (5th of 52). Jahmyr Gibbs was the engine, averaging 5.6 yards on 250 carries (+0.14 EPA per carry), while David Montgomery averaged 4.2 yards. Amon-Ra St. Brown had 141 targets, 115 catches, 1263 yards and +0.68 EPA per target. Play action from under center was used on 31% of dropbacks (1st of 32) for +0.43 EPA (4th of 32). The line allowed a 6% sack rate (9th of 32).

Aidan Hutchinson had 7.5 sacks and 28 pressures in 280 snaps, and Za'Darius Smith added 4 sacks. The team recorded 37 sacks (5% sack rate, 28th of 32) but produced 10.9 pressures per game (2nd of 32). The secondary was strong: the safeties ranked 1st of 32 in rating allowed (49.6) and the cornerbacks 8th (86.5). Special teams led the league at +5.4% DVOA, with Jake Bates making 26 of 29 field goals.

The 2024 Green Bay Packers went 11-6 with a point differential of +122, scoring 460 points (27.1 per game, 8th of 32) and allowing 338 (19.9 per game, 6th of 32). The offense ranked 8th of 32 in EPA per play (+0.08) and the defense 4th of 32 in EPA per play allowed (−0.06, where lower is better). Final FTN DVOA was 3rd of 32 overall at +24.5%: offense +17.3% (4th of 32), defense −7.1% (7th of 32, where lower is better), special teams +0.2% (15th of 32).

Jordan Love threw 25 touchdowns and 11 interceptions with a 96.7 rating and +0.13 EPA per dropback (16th of 52). Josh Jacobs ran 301 times for 1329 yards at 4.4 per carry, and Emanuel Wilson averaged 4.9 on 103 carries. Jayden Reed was the most efficient target at +0.55 EPA per target on 75 targets, and Tucker Kraft posted +0.53 on 70. Motion was a core tool, used on 63% of plays (4th of 32). The line allowed a 4% sack rate (3rd of 32).

Rashan Gary led the pass rush with 7.5 sacks, 15 QB hits and 25 pressures, with Devonte Wyatt adding 5 sacks. The team recorded 45 sacks (7% sack rate, 11th of 32). The safeties ranked 2nd of 32 in rating allowed (77.2), and the cornerbacks 9th (86.8), but the linebackers were weak in coverage at 104.0 (23rd of 32). Special teams were average, at +0.2% DVOA (15th of 32), though Keisean Nixon averaged 29.3 yards on 18 kick returns.

Houston finished 10-7 with a point differential of +0 (372 scored, 372 allowed). The offense ranked 23rd in EPA per play at −0.05, while the defense ranked 5th at −0.06. The final FTN DVOA table, which is the full-season figure, put the Texans 16th overall at +5.3%, 26th on offense at −12.4%, 3rd on defense at −15.3% (lower is better) and 8th on special teams at +2.3%. The defense carried a team whose offense ranked 31st in success rate (39%).

C.J. Stroud threw 20 touchdowns and 12 interceptions for an 87.0 rating, with EPA per dropback of −0.01 (33rd of 52) and a time to throw of 2.98 seconds (39th of 43). Nico Collins was the most efficient target (+0.43 EPA per target on 99 targets, 7 touchdowns), and Joe Mixon carried 245 times for 1016 yards at −0.05 EPA per carry. The line allowed a 27% pressure rate (32nd of 32) and an 8% sack rate (26th). Play action from under center was the strength (+0.25 gain, 5th).

Danielle Hunter led the defense with 12 sacks, 34 pressures and 23 QB hits, and Will Anderson added 11 sacks. The unit produced 49 sacks at an 8% sack rate (4th). Derek Stingley Jr. allowed a 51.2 rating with five interceptions, and the cornerbacks ranked 2nd with a 69.2 rating allowed, though linebackers ranked 25th at 106.3. Special teams ranked 8th at +2.3%, with Ka'imi Fairbairn 36 of 42 on field goals.

Indianapolis finished 8-9 with a point differential of −50 (377 scored, 427 allowed). The offense ranked 24th in EPA per play at −0.05, and the defense 13th at +0.00. The final FTN DVOA table, which is the full-season figure, put the Colts 19th overall at −7.1%, 20th on offense at −5.1%, 15th on defense at +0.9% (lower is better) and 21st on special teams at −1.1%. The quarterback position defined the year: Anthony Richardson's NGS CPOE of −11.2 was last in the league (43rd of 43).

Anthony Richardson threw 8 touchdowns and 12 interceptions for a 61.6 rating, with EPA per dropback of −0.11 (42nd of 52). Joe Flacco was steadier, with 12 touchdowns, 7 interceptions and +0.02 EPA per dropback (26th). Richardson's running was the most efficient rushing on the team (+0.23 EPA per carry on 58 carries). Alec Pierce was the most efficient target (+0.58 EPA per target, 7 touchdowns), and Jonathan Taylor ran 303 times for 1431 yards. Play action from under center was a disaster (−0.73 EPA, 32nd), and the line allowed a 23% pressure rate (23rd).

Kwity Paye led the defense with 8 sacks, and DeForest Buckner added 6.5 sacks and 14 QB hits. Laiatu Latu (team-high 23 pressures) and Dayo Odeyingbo (team-high 17 QB hits) helped produce 36 sacks, a 6% sack rate (23rd). The cornerbacks ranked 25th with a 99.2 rating, and Kenny Moore allowed five touchdowns. Special teams ranked 21st at −1.1%, with Matt Gay 31 of 37 on field goals.

Jacksonville finished 4-13 with a point differential of −115 (320 scored, 435 allowed). The offense ranked 18th in EPA per play at −0.02, but the defense ranked 31st at +0.13. The final FTN DVOA table, which is the full-season figure, put the Jaguars 26th overall at −17.7%, 17th on offense at −2.1%, 31st on defense at +18.6% (lower is better) and 6th on special teams at +3.0%. The defense was the collapse, allowing +0.23 EPA per dropback (32nd).

Trevor Lawrence threw 11 touchdowns and 7 interceptions, with EPA per dropback of +0.00 (31st of 52) and a CPOE of −3.3 (39th of 43). His 2.69-second time to throw ranked 7th quickest, but his 38% pressure-to-sack rate was above the league's 31%. Tank Bigsby (766 yards, +0.74 RYOE, 9th of 47) outproduced Travis Etienne (−0.18 EPA per carry). Brian Thomas Jr. was the top target (133 targets, 10 touchdowns, +0.41 EPA per target). The line allowed a 15% pressure rate (1st). Motion hurt the passing game: pass EPA of −0.12 (30th) with motion versus +0.07 (17th) without.

Travon Walker led the pass rush with 10.5 sacks and 29 pressures, and Josh Hines-Allen added 8 sacks and a team-high 19 QB hits. The unit recorded 34 sacks, a 5% sack rate (30th), and 6.6 pressures per game (29th). The secondary struggled: Montaric Brown allowed a 101.5 rating on 78 targets, and Ronald Darby allowed four touchdowns. Special teams were the bright spot at +3.0% (6th), with Cam Little 27 of 29 on field goals.

Kansas City went 15-2, scoring 385 points and allowing 326 for a differential of +59. The offense ranked 9th of 32 at an EPA per play of +0.07, and the defense ranked 15th at +0.01, where 1 means the lowest allowed. Final DVOA was +14.7%, 8th of 32: offense +10.8% (8th), defense −2.7% (12th) and special teams +1.2% (12th).

Patrick Mahomes posted an EPA per dropback of +0.16, 12th of 52, with 26 touchdowns and 11 interceptions, though his CPOE of −1.2 ranked 29th of 43. Kareem Hunt carried 200 times for 728 yards at 3.6 per carry. Travis Kelce drew 133 targets and Xavier Worthy 98 for 638 yards and 6 touchdowns. Justin Watson was the most efficient target at +0.60 on 32. The line allowed a 6% sack rate, 16th of 32, and a 21% pressure rate, 16th. Play action from under center produced an EPA of +0.25, 7th, on 8% of dropbacks.

George Karlaftis III led the pass rush with 8 sacks and a team-high 28 quarterback hits, Tershawn Wharton added 6.5 sacks, and Chris Jones had 5 sacks and the team-high 38 pressures. Kansas City totaled 39 sacks at a 6% rate, 22nd of 32, though it produced 9.5 pressures per game, 7th. In coverage the team passer rating allowed of 94.7 ranked 15th, and Trent McDuffie allowed a rating of 77.4 on 79 targets. Special teams finished 12th at +1.2%, with Harrison Butker making 21 of 25 field goals.

The 2024 Los Angeles Rams finished 10-7 over 17 games, scoring 367 points and allowing 386 for a point differential of −19. The offense ranked 15th in EPA per play at +0.02, and the defense ranked 25th at +0.04. The team averaged 21.6 points per game (20th of 32) and allowed 22.7 (17th of 32). Final full-season DVOA was +5.1% overall (17th of 32), +9.8% on offense (10th), +4.4% on defense (26th, where lower is better) and −0.2% on special teams (19th).

Matthew Stafford threw for 3762 yards with 20 TD and 8 INT over 517 attempts, with an NGS CPOE of −0.6 (27th of 43) and an EPA per dropback of +0.07 (20th of 52). Kyren Williams carried 316 times for 1299 yards. Puka Nacua had 106 targets, 990 yards and +0.49 EPA per target, and Cooper Kupp had 100 targets. Jordan Whittington was the most efficient target at +0.59 EPA per target on 28 targets. The offense allowed a 21% pressure rate (12th of 32) and a 5% sack rate (6th). Scheme note: the Rams used play action from under center on 25% of dropbacks (2nd), with +0.40 EPA on those plays (5th).

Braden Fiske led the defense with 8.5 sacks, Kobie Turner had 8 and Byron Young had 7.5. Jared Verse led the team with 29 pressures and 18 QB hits, adding 4.5 sacks. Cobie Durant allowed a 71.2 rating on 50 targets. The team passer rating allowed was 100.7 (22nd of 32), and the Edge/DL group allowed 115.3 (32nd).

The Chargers went 11-6, scoring 402 points and allowing 301 for a differential of +101. The offense ranked 12th of 32 at an EPA per play of +0.04, and the defense ranked 7th at −0.06, where 1 means the lowest allowed. Final DVOA was +12.6%, 9th of 32: offense +7.5% (12th), defense −5.0% (9th) and special teams +0.1% (16th).

Justin Herbert posted a CPOE of +2.4, 10th of 43, and an EPA per dropback of +0.13, 17th of 52, with 23 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. J.K. Dobbins carried 195 times for 905 yards at 4.6 per carry. Ladd McConkey was the most efficient target at +0.59 on 112 targets, with 1149 yards, while Quentin Johnston caught 8 touchdowns on 91 targets. The team used heavy sets on 31% of plays, 2nd of 32, with a heavy-set pass EPA of +0.38, 5th. The line allowed an 8% sack rate, 22nd, but committed just 22 penalties, 2nd fewest.

Tuli Tuipulotu led the defense with 8.5 sacks and 17 quarterback hits, Khalil Mack added 6 sacks and the team-high 22 pressures, and Bud Dupree had 6 sacks. The team totaled 46 sacks at a 7% rate, 9th of 32. In coverage, the team passer rating allowed of 92.3 ranked 10th, and yards per target allowed of 6.8 ranked 2nd of 32, while Tarheeb Still allowed a rating of 82.2 on 75 targets. Special teams were average, ranked 16th at +0.1%, while Cameron Dicker made 39 of 42 field goals.

Las Vegas went 4-13, scoring 309 points and allowing 434 for a differential of −125. The offense ranked 31st of 32 at an EPA per play of −0.14, while the defense ranked 19th at +0.02, where 1 means the lowest allowed. Final DVOA was −19.6%, 27th of 32: offense −17.8% (29th), defense +1.7% (18th) and special teams −0.1% (17th).

Gardner Minshew's EPA per dropback of −0.12 ranked 43rd of 52, while Aidan O'Connell threw 8 touchdowns with an aggressiveness of 21.0%, 2nd of 43. The run game was the core problem, with a rushing EPA of −0.28, ranked 32nd, and Alexander Mattison averaged 3.2 yards per carry on 132 carries. Brock Bowers was the top target with 153 targets and 1194 yards, and Jakobi Meyers added 129 targets for 1027 yards. Ameer Abdullah was the most efficient target at +0.25 on 47. The line allowed a 7% sack rate, 20th of 32, and a 22% pressure rate, 21st.

Maxx Crosby led the pass rush with 7.5 sacks, 20 quarterback hits and 28 pressures, while Adam Butler and K'Lavon Chaisson each added 5 sacks. The team totaled 38 sacks at a 6% rate, 21st of 32, and 7.5 pressures per game, 24th. The defense allowed a passer rating of 101.4, 25th of 32, and the linebacker group ranked 30th at 110.5. Defensive back penalties were low, 11 for 147 yards, tied for 2nd fewest. Special teams were below average at −0.1%, 17th, and Daniel Carlson made 34 of 40 field goals.

Miami finished 8-9 with a −19 point differential (345 points for, 364 against).
